rationale: C23 plausibly supplied a material immigration-counterterrorism drafting template. Both directives expressly respond to September 11 by adopting a national policy of preventing terrorist-associated aliens from entering the United States, then use coordinated visa screening, interagency intelligence and data sharing, enhanced immigration enforcement, program development, and timed presidential reporting. These parallels are substantially more concrete than a shared broad security topic. C19 has unusually close entry-suspension and national-interest-exception language, but it is embedded in a sanctions order and covers individually designated persons rather than countrywide screening. C12 is closely related in timing, style, and immigration administration, but primarily concerns unlawful southern-border entry rather than foreign-terrorist visa screening.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The visa-issuance process plays a crucial role in detecting individuals with terrorist ties and stopping them from entering the United States.... It is the policy of the United States to protect its citizens from foreign nationals who intend to commit terrorist attacks in the United States
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the attacks of September 11, 2001, showed that some come to the United States to commit terrorist acts.... It is the policy of the United States to work aggressively to prevent aliens who engage in or support terrorist activity from entering the United States
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel policy framing connects September 11, terrorist-associated aliens, and prevention of their entry.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Secretary of Homeland Security, in consultation with the Secretary of State and the Director of National Intelligence, shall immediately conduct a review to determine the information needed from any country to adjudicate any visa, admission, or other benefit under the INA
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Attorney General shall create the Foreign Terrorist Tracking Task Force... with assistance from the Secretary of State, the Director of Central Intelligence and other officers... [and] ensure that... Federal agencies coordinate programs to... deny entry into the United States of aliens associated with... terrorist activity
shared_material.explanation: Both establish coordinated immigration, intelligence, and diplomatic machinery to identify terrorist-associated aliens and prevent admission.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This program will include... a database of identity documents... amended application forms... a mechanism to ensure that the applicant is who the applicant claims to be; [and] a mechanism to assess whether or not the applicant has the intent to commit criminal or terrorist acts
shared_material.parent_excerpt: make recommendations about the use of advanced technology... to facilitate the rapid identification of aliens who are suspected of engaging in or supporting terrorist activity, to deny them access to the United States, and... maximize the ability of the government to detect, identify, locate, and apprehend potential terrorists
shared_material.explanation: The later order adapts the earlier directive's technology-and-data-based identification framework into detailed uniform visa-screening standards.
